proof.criterion: Every front-door container exits when the kubelet sends SIGTERM, so a replaced pod stops when its containers do, not at the 60 s grace period's SIGKILL (review round 2's important finding)
proof.surface: the advertiser and cert-publish scripts rendered in testdata/dispatch-tailnet-pod.golden (paths rewritten to temp dirs, a stub tailscale on PATH), each run as PID 1 of its own PID namespace (`unshare -Urpf --mount-proc`) under dash and under busybox sh 1.35, with SIGTERM sent from the parent namespace 3 s in
proof.observed: head-cert-publish: exited 0.00 s after SIGTERM, rc=0 (dash and busybox). head-advertiser: exited 0.00 s, rc=0 (dash and busybox). Both were inside a wait at the time (cert-publish in its 60 s publishing sleep), and neither left a process behind
proof.negativeControl: the same scripts rendered at c40c8634 (before the fix): rc=-15, killed by the default action because there is no handler, under both shells. On this gVisor host the signal reaches a PID 1 that has no handler; on Linux a container's PID 1 with no handler drops a signal sent from the host (pid_namespaces(7)). So rc 0 against rc -15 is the observable difference between a handler and none. The kernel drop itself cannot be reproduced here: gVisor delivers the signal and exposes no SigCgt in /proc/<pid>/status
